characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure consists of ferrite and austenite; peak intensity of austenite and ferrite shows almost no significant change after aging.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM equipped with EBSD detector; EBSD step size 300 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular-shaped ferrite dispersed in austenite matrix; ferrite content 16.4 vol% for 723 K/3 h; as-cast austenite grain size 18 μm, ferrite grain size 3.6 μm.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD scanning step size 300 nm; samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization, ferrite content and grain size measurement

characterization_methods.key_findings: Nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite, coherent [100]γ//[100]κ; NbC particles identified.
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JXA-8050G instrument at an electron beam voltage of 15 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Nb element uniformly dispersed within the austenite grain, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries.

Ferrite content 16.4 vol% for 0.02Nb steel 723 K/3 h.

characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify ferrite content, NbC particle size/volume fraction and κ-carbide size

characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 0.02Nb austenite grain size 18 μm; ferrite grain size 3.6 μm.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated phase constitution consistent with observed ferrite + austenite and NbC (MC) formation.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 2×2×2 atomic supercell of κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21); Nb at Fe face-centered position (Fe23NbAl8C8) or Al corner position (Fe24Al7NbC8); slab vacuum spacing 15 Å
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: PAW potentials; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV; U scheme 2.59 eV for Fe; kinetic energy cutoff 500 eV; 6×6×6 Monkhorst-Pack k-points
computational_details.simulation_method: Spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) within GGA-PBE
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Formation energies calculated: Fe24Al8C8 = 0.891 eV, Fe23NbAl8C8 = 2.826 eV, Fe24Al7NbC8 = 1.453 eV; Nb doping increases κ-carbide formation energy.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Al and C diffusion coefficients in austenite of 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, temperature range 673–873 K

Yield strength contributions assessed using Eqs (2)–(9); parameters M=3.06, α=0.23, b=0.26 nm, G=70 GPa (austenite); M_F=2, α_F=0.4, G_F=76 GPa (ferrite); Hall-Petch coefficient kγ=14.55 MPa·mm^-1/2; N=6, γ_APB=350 mJ/m^2
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated contributions reproduce the measured yield strength trend.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Nano-scale κ-carbides could be sheared by dislocations under plastic deformation (rather than Orowan looping).
NbC particles pin the movement of austenite grain boundaries during δ-ferrite → γ-austenite transformation, hindering austenite grain growth.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging at 723 K promotes intragranular κ-carbide formation/growth in austenite; no coarsened intergranular κ-carbides observed after aging at 723–823 K.
interfaces.slip_behavior: κ-carbides are sheared by dislocations during plastic deformation (small-size regime).

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: 0.04Nb steel yield strength exceeds 0.02Nb steel by ≈71 MPa (912 ± 11 vs 983 ± 13 MPa at 723 K/3 h)

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification (induction melting in water-cooled copper crucible, re-melting and pouring into rotating copper mold)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel strips of 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm obtained by near-rapid solidification; parent (as-cast) state of the aged sample.
723 K was selected as the aging temperature giving better comprehensive mechanical properties for extended aging studies.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness tester (MH-5L); indentation load 200 gf; holding time 20 s
MTS Criterion 44 universal testing machine; minimum four repetitions per steel strip
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for 723 K/3 h (red curve in Figure 9a): steep elastic rise followed by flat plastic plateau around ~1000–1050 MPa, terminating near 31% strain.

samples.sample_label: 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 3 h

phases_present.grain_size: 18 μm (as-cast value; aging leaves austenite grain size almost unchanged)

size.value: nano-scale (2.0 nm in as-cast; grows with aging, reaching 7.8 nm at 823 K)

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase microstructure consisting of ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ); irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix.
